scope: v4 implemented local character/studio/signature study: visual association cues and readiness for a defensible future audience study. This is an AI craft/research-readiness judgment, not a human response score, deployment approval, or normal-speed motion assessment.
independence: Saved before reading the partner new review or score. Prior own-role expanded-panel record was read for continuity.

brand/animation-v5/character.js: render geometry, gaze, mittens, glasses and face channels
evidenceActuallyInspected.versionCheck: SHA-256 matched v4 for signature HTML/JS/CSS, motion.js, character.js, studio.js, index.html and comparison.mp4.
evidenceActuallyInspected.videoInspection: Read exact-engine 30 fps / 2664-frame / 88.8-second export metadata and inspected decoded Investigation & sharing sheets in both themes. Did not watch continuous normal-speed playback.

score.meaning: Strong, coherent visual association material and unusually clear evidence boundaries; not yet a neutral, exposure-controlled audience research stimulus. Ordinal specialist judgment within this narrow inspected scope, not an empirical success rate.

audienceOutcomes.reason: No unfamiliar human participants or measured memory outcomes. Nag choosing Investigate & share establishes personal fit only.

strengths: The same small head/body/antenna/wing language survives the current theme and size sheet. The header visibly couples the character with heyNag; README then supplies first-person software work. This gives future recall research a specific owner-name association to test.

Investigation has an actual subject: the eva.md memory question. Source and inspected sequence distinguish noticing, glasses/consideration, and returning to a modest presenting mitten. It offers a plausible memory story without inventing a project success claim.

The current portrait stage gives the unchanged character more visible room, and the question remains above/right. Both 390px stage images retain the face, four-wing silhouette and modest hand gesture.

The study exposes choice, timeline inspection, still state and reduced-motion behavior; it preserves the selected owner direction and separates comparison studies from the 24-emotion catalogue. These are useful reproducible authoring controls.

deductions.severity: medium within research-readiness scope; nonblocking for the authoring study
deductions.finding: The Performance labels, curiosity heading, Compare the intent explanation, emotion labels and decoded-sheet captions disclose the intended interpretation. Reusing these as an unprimed comprehension test would confound the response with the supplied answer.
deductions.basis: signature.html; studio.js; all-final.png; decoded-day-5.png and decoded-night-5.png
deductions.action: For any later comprehension experiment, use a separate neutral presentation of the selected clip at its intended size. Ask a free description before revealing variant names or trait choices; retain accessible descriptions appropriate to the research question rather than silently stripping accessibility.

deductions.severity: low to medium within cross-device research-readiness scope
deductions.finding: The 320px initial viewport shows the brand and project question before the character enters view; the 390px stage capture begins after scrolling and omits the heyNag navigation. Those are different exposures. Recall differences across such captures cannot be attributed solely to the character or theme.
deductions.basis: signature-final-320.png compared with signature-final-390-stage.png and signature-final-1440.png
deductions.confidence: high for visible framing; no claim about actual browsing behavior
deductions.action: Record viewport, scroll position, whether the moth and name were actually seen, exposure length and playback use. For a focused comparison hold those conditions constant; for natural browsing retain the difference and report it.

deductions.finding: The final sharing mitten is visible at the portrait-stage size but remains a small change near the collar and glasses-dominated face. At the 96px full-body sample it is a weak independent cue for sharing. The artwork supports warm attention more confidently than a specific social action without context.
deductions.confidence: medium for this reviewer’s static reading; human interpretation and timing unknown
deductions.action: Test only the consequential distinction (investigates then invites/shares versus merely looks/thinks). If it repeatedly fails, try staging or timing first; do not enlarge hands or distort the selected anatomy preemptively.

improvementCriteria: Prepare a neutral single-direction exposure for the specific comprehension question, with version, size, theme and duration recorded and labels revealed only after the free description.

Define separate outcomes for recalling heyNag, recalling the visual, linking the two, identifying software work, and liking the character. Ask unaided recall before recognition alternatives; retain verbatim dissent and denominators.
Use natural profile exposure for owner/work association, and unlabeled silent clips for isolated action comprehension. Do not combine their findings into a single attachment number.

A stronger craft score could follow evidence that the small sharing cue remains readable at its intended production size, including continuous playback review. Actual audience-outcome scores would require relevant human observations; their absence does not block this local implementation.
confidence: Moderate for the narrow craft/readiness score; high for source, labels and framing observations; no confidence assigned to unmeasured audience outcomes.

implementedAssessment.accepted: Current v4 local implementation as an owner-selected, inspectable character/curiosity study with preserved tiny identity and useful project context.

limits: AI specialist evidence, not independent human research. No recruited observers, recall task or audience preference results.
No browser operated in this role; root owns the TaskSpace. Operability records were inspected, not personally reproduced.
Decoded frames and export cadence do not establish normal-speed perceptual continuity; no live smoothness endorsement.
Desktop narrow screenshots and coarse-pointer emulation do not establish real-device input zoom, touch feel, safe areas or keyboard behavior.
Source ARIA descriptions and native AX records do not establish screen-reader spoken output. Native dropdown keyboard commit is explicitly inconclusive in the supplied evidence.
The project-cue verification record was inspected; no separate upstream project audit was performed.

skillsReviewed.application: Applied emil-design-eng evidence/craft separation and mobile-native hardware boundary; inspected prototype for future comparison workflow. No new prototype build was invoked.

workflowChanges: Before review, state whether the decision is owner preference, expert craft, usability, comprehension or memory. The same variant picker cannot answer all five.

Future website explorations should name a real axis, show one fully working direction at realistic size/context, keep switching immediate and preserve the owner choice. Separately prepare neutral randomized/counterbalanced exposure when a research question requires it.

Version and log the actual exposure: source hash, device class, viewport, crop/scroll, theme, playback/still state and motion preference. Pair discussions must keep screenshot claims separate from hardware and human claims.
Keep intentional character timing and small anatomy. Apply UI frequency/feedback guidance to controls; judge the character story through its own beats and rendered evidence.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Prototype requires its exact picker and stops for a selection.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: This is an independent review, not an invoked variant-building run; Nag already selected Investigate & share. No extra picker, source edit or permission pause is warranted.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Prototype cleanup deletes an exploration after selection.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: Repository instructions require retaining historical comparison evidence. Preserve it as historical, not current production artwork.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Never animate keyboard actions; all UI motion stays under 300ms.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: Keyboard Play deliberately requests character content. Immediate control feedback and full accessible playback coexist; the 4.1-second performance is intentional content, not UI delay.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Only transform/opacity; add stagger or blur to polish.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: SVG face/antenna changes express the selected character. No evidence here justifies replacing expressive geometry, adding decorative stagger, or blurring a subtle comprehension cue. Measure the relevant workload before performance changes.

rulesNotApplicableWithReason.rule: Apply all mobile-native baseline CSS globally.
rulesNotApplicableWithReason.reason: This is a scrolling document/study. Zoom, selectable content, normal link feedback and scrolling remain useful; physical-device claims remain open without hardware.
The required independent output is JSON and no UI patch is proposed; a compact Before/After table is retained below for the actual workflow changes rather than substituting a generic code audit.

workflowBeforeAfterMarkdown:
| Before | After | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Treat named variant choice as evidence of audience understanding | Record it as Nag personal-fit preference; use neutral free response for comprehension | The displayed names supply the intended reading |
| Compare narrow screenshots as equal exposures | Log viewport, scroll, name/moth visibility and playback | Portrait ordering changes what a visitor can see |
| Call emulation a mobile result | Keep code/layout checks separate from physical-device findings | Touch, keyboard and browser chrome need hardware |
